kernel_events.asserts: Exact report contents and order, selected bus transactions, bounds on observed delays, and identical printed traces including raw ticks per case in tests/kernel/events/cases.json. Real devicetree instances, I2C emulator, ISR-raised RDY, work and input queues, PM and ZMK listener. Fixture/case-list equality and successful retained list subprocess required. Product runs: both cores, one build at the production 32768 Hz tick rate, every case three times on that binary. Identity covers src, fixture, Kconfig, dts, CMakeLists.txt, zephyr and dependencies.json; dependency selection rechecked after execution.
kernel_events.negative_control: --negative-control mutations: the unchanged 32768 Hz baseline runs concurrently with the --jobs workers and must pass every named case with three identical-binary repeats for the control to succeed. Every worker must finish successfully; pristine-build failures and exceptions with tracebacks are terminal failures recorded in results.json alongside baseline_passed and mutations. Workers each build a pristine copy once, retaining its SHA-256, .config, zephyr.dts and CMakeCache.txt under worker-N/, then apply one fault at a time, rebuild incrementally, run its named cases and restore the file. Every successful rebuild records the executable SHA-256; equality with the worker's pristine hash is STALE-BINARY, fails and skips cases. Every non-REJECTED fault retains the available executable; failed rebuild logs remain. Each fault applies with the exact match count within the function body or whole file, must build, and must be rejected by an entire IQSFAIL case=NAME line=NUMBER assertion line and exit 1 from every named case. Timeouts, signals, other exits, similarly named cases, build failures, stale binaries, survivors and faults that never ran fail, reported separately from product runs.
kernel_events.output_isolation: Normalize evidence paths before writes; reject owner, workspace and every selected west project root, including aliases and uncloned roots. Existing evidence, source bytes and source directory trees stay untouched. External siblings and safe aliases remain supported. test_runner.py drives the actual entry with synthetic dependencies and builds, including discarded dot-dot components, normalized existing targets and symlink loops.
kernel_events.limits: Model only: no capacitive front end, gesture classifier, forced-communication clock stretching, wake reseed, electrical timing/bus, contention, keyboard input processors or elapsed time on a board
kernel_events.model: Datasheet v1.4: programmed 0x32 window timeout discards window gesture flags/pending report while preserving the current sample for forced/verification reads (100 ms assumed before programming; no documented default), STOP ends session, Show Reset gates event mode, bits 9/10 gate gesture/trackpad events, one-cycle re-ATI, suspend after session. Backpressure: 17 accepted reports, ninth contact read blocks, three independently timed-out windows; all 19 produced contact reports, later lift and triple tap delivered in order. Present sensors finish with no contact/verification work and quiet bus; absent sensors at most three boot attempts. Stationary verified-contact backpressure: expired window and due verification during stall; resume gives exactly 21 reports with contact held, then normal lift gives 24. timeout-invents-lift restores zeroing and must be rejected separately as a model control.

kernel.asserts: Actual ordinary/delayed work and full-queue input consumer reject synchronous PM with EWOULDBLOCK before side effects; subsequent external suspend/resume releases the owed button exactly once. Three cases x three identical-binary runs per core. Actual Zephyr conversion comparison at 7 positive rates over all 65536 uint16 waits; existing PM markers and behavior retained.

kernel.limits: Actual kernel cancellation with GPIO emulation; no physical bus, sensor or downstream transport evidence

timeout_conversion: Two variable touch verification reservations use 32-bit divisions with exact ceiling over the full uint16 range, retaining the tick ABI, zero-disable behavior and all I2C/GPIO/PM/report policy. No retired instrumentation.

raw_tap_cells.asserts: Actual raw32-bit DTS tap cells: explicit <(-1)> means disabled for all3 tap properties; default -1 and valid0/127 stay accepted. Each property rejects -2,128,255,256,65535 with exactly its named compile assertion. Source object compilation uses pinned clean stock/DYA; before repair explicit disabled fails the single-tap assertion on both. No runtime gesture/click/lifecycle logic changed.
